results.title: Modus ponens for provability from sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, if $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$ and $S$ proves $\varphi$, then $S$ proves $\psi$.

results.title: Ex falso for provability from sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. If $S$ proves $\bot$, then $S$ proves every formula $\varphi$.

results.title: Deduction theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be such formulas. If $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ proves $\psi$, then $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$.

results.title: Consistent set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $\alpha$ a type of variables. A set $S$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is consistent when $S$ does not prove $\bot$.

results.title: Provability as inconsistency with the negation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\neg\varphi\}$ is not consistent.

results.title: Refutability as inconsistency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\neg\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ is not consistent.

results.title: Unions of chains of consistent sets are consistent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $C$ is a nonempty family of sets of formulas that is totally ordered by inclusion and every member of $C$ is consistent, then the union $\bigcup C$ is consistent.

results.title: Maximal consistent set
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A set $\Delta$ of formulas is maximal consistent when it is consistent and every consistent set of formulas containing $\Delta$ is contained in $\Delta$, that is, equals $\Delta$.

results.title: Maximal consistent sets absorb consistent extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas of a language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. If $\Delta \cup \{\varphi\}$ is consistent, then $\varphi \in \Delta$.

results.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for first-order logic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every consistent set $S$ of first-order formulas is contained in a maximal consistent set.

results.title: Maximal consistent sets of first-order formulas are deductively closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. Every formula $\varphi$ that $\Delta$ proves lies in $\Delta$.

results.title: Universal instantiation in maximal consistent sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $t$ write $\varphi(t)$ for the result of substituting $t$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains $\forall x\, \varphi$, then $\Delta$ contains $\varphi(t)$ for every term $t$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $u$ write $\varphi(u)$ for the result of substituting $u$ for $x$. results.title: Henkin axiom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open and let $c$ be a variable; write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. The Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is the formula $\neg \forall x\, \varphi \to \neg \varphi(c)$.

results.title: Adding a Henkin axiom preserves consistency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $S$ be a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and let $c \in \alpha$ be a variable that occurs free neither in $\varphi$ nor in any formula of $S$. Then $S$ together with the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is consistent.

results.title: Universal formulas from Henkin witnesses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, let $c \in \alpha$, and write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ and contains $\varphi(c)$, then $\Delta$…

results.title: Free variables of an instance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term and $\varphi$ a first-order formula with $m + 1$ bound variables, and let $\varphi(t)$ be the instance obtained by substituting $t$ for the outermost bound variable. Every free variable of $\varphi(t)$ is a free variable of $\varphi$ or a variable of $t$.

results.title: Depth of a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The depth $d(\varphi)$ of a first-order formula $\varphi$ is the nesting height of its implications and universal quantifiers: $\bot$, equations and relation atoms have depth $0$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ has depth $\max(d(\varphi), d(\psi)) + 1$, and $\forall \varphi$ has depth $d(\varphi) + 1$.

results.title: Renaming depends only on the free variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables, let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ further variables reserved for binding by enclosing quantifiers. If two maps $f, g : \alpha \to \beta$ agree on every variable from $\alpha$ that occurs free in $\varphi$, then renaming the variables of $\varphi$ from $\alpha$ along $f$ and along $g$ gives the same formula.

results.title: Renaming free variables along an arbitrary map preserves derivability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables with $\beta$ infinite, and let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ be any map. If $\varphi$ is derivable from the list of hypotheses $\Gamma$ in natural deduction, then the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by renaming each free variable $x$ to $f(x)$ is derivable from the list obtained by renaming the free variables of each formula of $\Gamma$ in the same way.

results.title: Doubling the variables preserves consistency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $S$ is a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, then the set obtained from $S$ by renaming every free variable $x$ to $2x$ in each of its formulas is consistent.

results.title: Replacing arguments one at a time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r$ be a relation on a type $\beta$, let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a property of $n$-tuples $x = (x_i)_{i < n}$ in $\beta$. Suppose that for every tuple $x$, every position $i$ and all $a, b \in \beta$ with $r(a, b)$, if $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $a$, then $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $b$. results.title: Congruence for function symbols in a maximal consistent set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be an $n$-ary function symbol, let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be terms over $\mathbb{N}$ and let $i < n$. For a term $u$, write $x[i := u]$ for $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $u$. If the equation $a = b$ lies in $\Delta$, then the equation $f(x[i := a]) = f(x[i := b])$ lies in $\Delta$.

results.title: Replacing an argument of a relation symbol by an equal term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be an $n$-ary relation symbol, let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, $a$ and $b$ be terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $i < n$. If $\Delta$ contains $a = b$ and contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $a$, then $\Delta$ contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $b$.

results.title: Term structure of a set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. The term structure of $\Delta$ is the $L$-structure whose domain is the set of $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in which an $n$-ary function symbol $f$ sends terms $t_1, \dots, t_n$ to the term $f(t_1, \dots, t_n)$, and an $n$-ary relation symbol $R$ holds of $t_1, \dots, t_n$ exactly when the atomic…

results.title: Provable equality of terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. Provable equality in $\Delta$ is the equivalence relation on $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ under which $s \sim t$ holds exactly when the equation $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.

results.title: Term model of a maximal consistent set
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the term model of $\Delta$ is the set of terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ modulo the equivalence relation that identifies $s$ and $t$ when the formula $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.

results.title: Canonical assignment of the term model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the canonical assignment sends each variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ to $[x]$, the class of the variable term $x$ in the term model of $\Delta$.

results.title: Lowering a term with no bound variables
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A term whose variables are free variables from $\mathbb{N}$ together with bound variables from the empty index set is lowered to the term over $\mathbb{N}$ of the same shape, in which every free variable $x$ stays $x$.

results.title: Enumeration of formulas with one bound variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the formulas $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ are a fixed enumeration, chosen by choice, of all first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and one bound variable: every such formula is $\varphi_k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Variable bound of a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a first-order formula whose variables are natural numbers together with $n$ variables reserved for quantifiers. Its variable bound $b(\varphi)$ is one more than the largest natural number occurring as a free variable of $\varphi$, or $1$ when there is none; it is a strict upper bound on these free variables.

results.title: Witness bases
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with countably many symbols, let $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ be the fixed surjective enumeration of the $L$-formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and one variable reserved for a quantifier, and let $b(\varphi)$ be one more than the largest free variable of $\varphi$, or $1$ if it has none. The witness bases are defined by $w_0 = b(\varphi_0)$ and…

results.title: Henkin witnesses
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with countably many symbols and let $w_0 < w_1 < \dots$ be its witness bases, built from the fixed enumeration $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ of the $L$-formulas with one variable reserved for a quantifier. results.title: The $k$-th Henkin axiom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a language with countably many symbols and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th Henkin axiom is the Henkin axiom $\neg \forall \varphi_k \to \neg \varphi_k(c_k)$, where $\varphi_k$ is the $k$-th formula in the enumeration of formulas with one bound variable and $c_k$ is the $k$-th Henkin witness.

results.title: Stages of the Henkin extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in a language with countably many symbols, and let $H_k$ be the $k$-th Henkin axiom. The stages $S_k$ are defined by $S_0 = S$ and $S_{k+1} = S_k \cup \{H_k\}$, so $S_k$ is $S$ together with $H_0, \dots, H_{k-1}$.

results.title: Henkin extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the Henkin extension of a set $S$ of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is $S$ together with all Henkin axioms, the $k$-th Henkin axiom for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Henkin extension of a consistent set

results.title: Model existence for first-order logic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many symbols. Every consistent set $S$ of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is satisfiable: there are a nonempty $L$-structure $M$, in the universe of the function symbols of $L$, and an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to M$ under which every formula of $S$ holds.

Let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$, all with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. results.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many function and relation symbols, whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$. Let $T$ be a theory of $L$ and $\varphi$ a formula of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. results.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many function and relation symbols, whose function symbols live in universe $u$ and relation symbols in universe $v$. For every theory $T$ of $L$ and every formula $\varphi$ of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, $\varphi$ is provable from the sentences of $T$, viewed as formulas over $\mathbb{N}$, if and only if $\varphi$ holds under every assignment of the variables in…

results.title: Finite set of symbols of a term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite set of symbols occurring in a term $t$ of a first-order language $L$, a finite subset of the function and relation symbols of $L$, is defined by recursion on $t$: it is empty when $t$ is a variable, and when $t = f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$ for an $l$-ary function symbol $f$ it consists of $f$ together with the symbols occurring in each of $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$.

results.title: The head function symbol of a term occurs in it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $f$ an $l$-ary function symbol of $L$, and $t_1, \dots, t_l$ $L$-terms with variables in $\alpha$. Then $f$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in the term $f(t_1, \dots, t_l)$.

results.title: Symbols of an argument of a function application
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an $l$-ary function symbol of a first-order language $L$ and let $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$ be terms of $L$ in variables from $\alpha$. For every $i < l$, every symbol occurring in $t_i$ occurs in the term $f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$: the finite set of symbols of $t_i$ is contained in that of $f(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$.

results.title: Finite set of symbols of a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite set of function and relation symbols occurring in a bounded formula of a first-order language $L$, defined by recursion on the formula: $\bot$ has no symbols; an equation $t_1 = t_2$ has the function symbols of $t_1$ and $t_2$; an atomic formula $R(t_1, \dots, t_l)$ has $R$ together with the function symbols of $t_1, \dots, t_l$; an implication $\varphi \to \psi$ has the symbols of $\varphi$ and of…

results.title: Symbols of the left side of an equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and let $t_1$, $t_2$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Every symbol occurring in $t_1$ occurs in the atomic formula $t_1 = t_2$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_1$ is contained in that of $t_1 = t_2$.

results.title: Symbols of the right side of an equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and let $t_1$, $t_2$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Every symbol occurring in $t_2$ occurs in the atomic formula $t_1 = t_2$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_2$ is contained in that of $t_1 = t_2$.

results.title: The relation symbol of an atomic formula occurs in it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $R$ an $l$-ary relation symbol of $L$, and $t_1, \dots, t_l$ $L$-terms with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. Then $R$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in the atomic bounded formula $R(t_1, \dots, t_l)$.

results.title: Symbols of an argument of a relational atomic formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be an $l$-ary relation symbol of a first-order language $L$ and let $t_0, \dots, t_{l-1}$ be terms of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. For every $i < l$, every symbol occurring in $t_i$ occurs in the atomic formula $R(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$, viewed as a formula with $n$ bound variables: the finite set of symbols of $t_i$ is contained in that of $R(t_0, \dots, t_{l-1})$.

results.title: Symbols of the antecedent occur in an implication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For bounded formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables, every symbol occurring in $\varphi$ occurs in $\varphi \to \psi$.

results.title: Symbols of the consequent occur in an implication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For bounded formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables, every symbol occurring in $\psi$ occurs in $\varphi \to \psi$.

results.title: Symbols of a finite set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $F$ of first-order formulas of a language $L$ with free variables indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, the symbols of $F$ are the finite set of function and relation symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$, that is, the union over $\psi \in F$ of the finite sets of symbols occurring in $\psi$.

results.title: A symbol of a member of a set of formulas is a symbol of the set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $F$ a finite set of $L$-formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and $\psi \in F$. Every symbol occurring in $\psi$ belongs to the finite set of symbols occurring in some formula of $F$.

results.title: Sublanguage of a finite set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $F$ of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ has as its $n$-ary function symbols the $n$-ary function symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$, and as its $n$-ary relation symbols the $n$-ary relation symbols of $L$ that occur in some formula of $F$.

results.title: Inclusion of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For a finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, this is the language homomorphism from the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ into $L$ that sends each function symbol and each relation symbol to itself.

results.title: The inclusion of the sublanguage of a finite set of formulas is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language. For every finite set $F$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the inclusion into $L$ of the sublanguage of $L$ on the symbols occurring in $F$ is injective on function symbols and on relation symbols.

results.title: Term substitution depends only on the values of the substitution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $s$ be a term of $L$ with variables in a type $\beta$, and let $g$ and $g'$ assign to each variable in $\beta$ a term of $L$ with variables in a type $\gamma$. If $g(a) = g'(a)$ for every $a \in \beta$, then substituting $g$ into $s$ gives the same term as substituting $g'$ into $s$.

results.title: Language homomorphisms preserve the free variables of a term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\phi : L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages and let $t$ be a term of $L$ in free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. The finite set of free variables from $\alpha$ occurring in the image $\phi(t)$ of $t$ under $\phi$ equals the finite set of those occurring in $t$.

results.title: Language homomorphisms preserve free variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h : L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages, and let $\varphi$ be a bounded formula of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. The formula of $L'$ obtained from $\varphi$ by replacing each symbol by its image under $h$ has the same free variables as $\varphi$.

results.title: Language homomorphisms preserve equations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h \colon L \to L'$ be a homomorphism of first-order languages. For an $L$-term or $L$-formula $x$, write $h(x)$ for the term or formula of $L'$ obtained by replacing every symbol by its image under $h$. If $s$ and $t$ are $L$-terms with free variables in $\alpha$, then $h$ applied to the formula $s = t$ is the formula $h(s) = h(t)$.

A vertex $v$ is critical for $G'$ if $\{v\}$ is a critical vertex set of $G'$, that is, deleting $v$ from $G'$ strictly lowers the chromatic number of $G'$, viewed as a graph on its own vertex set, with chromatic numbers taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.

results.title: Vertex-critical graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A graph $G$ is $k$-critical (or vertex-critical) if its chromatic number equals $k$ and every vertex $v$ of $G$ is critical, that is, deleting $v$ from $G$ strictly lowers the chromatic number.

results.title: Cocolorable graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A graph $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors if there is a map from its vertices to the colors $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that each color class induces either an independent set or a complete graph in $G$.

results.title: Colorable graphs are cocolorable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, if a graph $G$ has a proper coloring with $n$ colors, then $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors.

results.title: Finite graphs are cocolorable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ is cocolorable with $|V|$ colors.

results.title: Cochromatic number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cochromatic number of a graph $G$, an element of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, is the least natural number $n$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors, that is, the least number of colors in a coloring of the vertices of $G$ in which each color class induces either an independent set or a complete graph. It is $\infty$ exactly when $G$ is not cocolorable with any finite number of colors.

results.title: Cochromatic number as a minimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a graph $G$ is cocolorable with $n$ colors for some natural number $n$, then the cochromatic number of $G$ equals the least natural number $m$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $m$ colors.

results.title: Cochromatic number of a finite graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the cochromatic number of $G$, converted from $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ to $\mathbb{N}$ by sending $\infty$ to $0$, equals the least natural number $m$ such that $G$ is cocolorable with $m$ colors.

results.title: Chromatic cardinal of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The chromatic cardinal is the minimal number of colors need to color it. In contrast to `chromaticNumber`, which assigns `⊤ : ℕ∞` to all non-finitely colorable graphs, this definition returns a `Cardinal` and can therefore distinguish between different infinite chromatic numbers.

results.title: Largest union of independent sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a natural number $k$, this is the maximum number of vertices in a union of $k$ (possibly empty, possibly overlapping) independent sets of $G$.

results.title: CDS-colorable graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A graph $G$ on a finite vertex set is CDS-colorable if it has a proper coloring $C$ with colors in $\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of vertices whose color under $C$ is less than $k$ equals the maximum size of a union of $k$ independent sets of $G$.

results.title: Rainbow homomorphisms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a graph homomorphism from $H$ to $G$ and let $c$ be a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of a type $K$. Then $f$ is rainbow for $c$ if distinct edges of $H$ are mapped to edges of $G$ with distinct labels, that is, the labeling $e \mapsto c(f(e))$ of the edges of $H$ is injective.

results.title: Powers of a unital endomorphism fix the constant function

It is a linear…

results.title: Wright–Fisher step is the Bernstein operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `wfStep M` is the Bernstein approximation operator.

results.title: One Wright–Fisher generation is a sup-norm contraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One Wright–Fisher generation is a contraction for the sup norm.

results.title: One Wright–Fisher generation fixes constants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One Wright–Fisher generation fixes the constant function `1`.

results.title: One Wright–Fisher generation preserves nonnegativity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One Wright–Fisher generation maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions.

results.title: Iterated Wright–Fisher generations are sup-norm contractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Any number of Wright–Fisher generations is a contraction for the sup norm.

results.title: Moment duality, one generation (polynomial identity)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `M ≥ 1` gene copies, `∑_i C(M, i) x^i (1 - x)^(M - i) (i/M)^n = ∑_k S(n, k) M_(k) / M^n · x^k`: the `n`-th moment of the frequency after one generation equals the generating function of the number of distinct parents of `n` sampled genes. Holds for every real `x`.

results.title: Moment duality, one generation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the allele count after one neutral Wright–Fisher generation with `M ≥ 1` gene copies is `Bin(M, x)`, then `E_x[(X₁)^n] = ∑_k wfLineageProb M n k · x^k`, where `X₁` is the new frequency and `wfLineageProb M n k` is the probability that `n` genes have `k` distinct parents.

results.title: One Wright–Fisher generation acting on monomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One generation maps `x ^ n` to `∑_k wfLineageProb M n k x ^ k`.

results.title: Moment duality, `m` generations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `M ≥ 1` and `n ≤ N`, `m` generations of the Wright–Fisher chain map `x ^ n` to `∑_k ((wfLineageMatrix N M)^m) n k · x^k`: the `n`-th moment of the frequency after `m` generations is the generating function of the number of ancestors, `m` generations back, of `n` sampled genes.

results.title: Dual moment polynomial of Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dual moment polynomial `∑_k P_t(n → k) X^k`, where for `t ≥ 0`, `P_t(n → k) = exp (t • G) n k` is the probability that `n` lineages of Kingman's coalescent have `k` ancestors time `t` earlier (time in units of `M = 2N` generations); evaluated at `x` it is `E_n[x^{A_t}]` for the block-counting process `A`.

results.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup on polynomials by moment duality
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup on polynomials, defined by moment duality on the monomial basis: `polySemigroup t (X ^ n) = dualMomentPoly t n`. It is meaningful for `t ≥ 0`; the formula is defined, and the group law holds, for every real `t`.

results.title: Dual semigroup on a monomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dual semigroup on a monomial is the dual moment polynomial.

results.title: Dual semigroup at time zero is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At time `0` the dual semigroup is the identity.

results.title: Semigroup law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Semigroup law on polynomials, from `exp ((s + t) • G) = exp (t • G) * exp (s • G)` and truncation consistency; holds for all real `s`, `t`.

results.title: Dual semigroup fixes the constant polynomial one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dual semigroup fixes the constant polynomial `1` (zero lineages stay zero).

results.title: Convergence on polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `t ≥ 0` and every polynomial `p`, `⌊tM⌋` generations of the Wright–Fisher chain with `M` gene copies applied to `p` converge uniformly on `[0, 1]` to `polySemigroup t p` as `M → ∞` (moment duality plus Kingman's theorem for the lineage count).

results.title: Rescaled Wright–Fisher iterates form a Cauchy sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every continuous `f`, the sequence `(wfStep M)^⌊tM⌋ f` is Cauchy in `C([0, 1], ℝ)`: it converges on the dense set of polynomials and the operators are contractions.

results.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup on `C([0, 1], ℝ)`, time in units of `M = 2N` generations: `wfSemigroup t f` is the uniform limit of `(wfStep M)^⌊tM⌋ f` as `M → ∞` (`tendsto_wfStep_pow_floor`). For `t < 0` it is the identity (a junk value: `⌊tM⌋₊ = 0`).

results.title: Diffusion approximation of the transition operators (Trotter–Kato, concrete form)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every continuous `f`, `⌊tM⌋` generations of the neutral Wright–Fisher chain with `M` gene copies applied to `f` converge uniformly on `[0, 1]` to `wfSemigroup t f`.

results.title: Contraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `sup_{[0,1]} |wfSemigroup t f| ≤ sup_{[0,1]} |f|`.

results.title: Diffusion semigroup agrees with the dual semigroup on polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On polynomials the diffusion semigroup is the dual semigroup, for `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup at nonpositive times is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `t ≤ 0`, `wfSemigroup t` is the identity (at `t = 0` by definition of a semigroup; for `t < 0` this is a junk value of the definition).

results.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup at time zero is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At time `0` the diffusion semigroup is the identity.

results.title: Moment duality for the diffusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Moment duality for the diffusion (Ethier & Griffiths 1993). For `t ≥ 0`, the semigroup applied to `x ↦ x ^ n` is `∑_k P_t(n → k) x^k`, with `P_t = exp (t • G)` the transition matrix of Kingman's block-counting process `A`; in process language `E_x[(X_t)^n] = E_n[x^{A_t}]` (the processes themselves are not constructed here).

results.title: Semigroup law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Semigroup law for `s, t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion semigroup fixes constants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The diffusion semigroup fixes constants (it is Markov: total mass `1`).

results.title: Positivity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The diffusion semigroup maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions.

results.title: Strong continuity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `wfSemigroup t f → f` uniformly as `t → 0⁺`, for every continuous `f`.

results.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher generator on polynomials

results.title: Generator on polynomials

results.summary: For every polynomial `p`, `(wfSemigroup t p - p) / t → x (1 - x) / 2 · p''` uniformly on `[0, 1]` as `t → 0⁺`.

results.title: Polynomial semigroup dynamics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At every positive time, differentiating the existing Wright–Fisher semigroup on a polynomial equals applying the semigroup to its generator.

results.title: Second-moment bound for the Wright–Fisher semigroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The centered second moment grows at most linearly: `T_t[(y-x)²](x) ≤ t/4`.

results.title: Fourth-moment Kolmogorov bound for the Wright–Fisher semigroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fourth centered increment of the neutral Wright–Fisher semigroup satisfies the uniform Kolmogorov bound `T_t[(y-x)⁴](x) ≤ (3/16)t²`.

results.title: Wright–Fisher semigroup as a positive operator

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Positive Wright–Fisher operator fixes constants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The positive Wright–Fisher operator fixes the constant function `1`.

results.title: Semigroup law for the positive Wright–Fisher operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The positive-operator form of the Wright–Fisher semigroup law.

results.title: Transition kernel of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The transition kernel of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion at time `t`. For nonnegative `t` it is the probabilistic transition corresponding to `wfSemigroup t`; for negative `t`, both the operator and kernel are the identity junk value inherited from `wfSemigroup`.

results.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel represents the semigroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Integration against the transition kernel agrees with the Wright–Fisher semigroup on every continuous test function and every initial allele frequency.

results.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel is the identity at nonpositive times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonpositive times, the Wright–Fisher transition is the identity kernel.

results.title: Wright–Fisher transition kernel is the identity at time zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At time zero the Wright–Fisher transition is the identity kernel.

results.title: Wright–Fisher transitions at time zero are Dirac masses

results.summary: Pointwise identity law for the transition kernel at time zero.

results.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for the Wright–Fisher diffusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Chapman–Kolmogorov law for the Wright–Fisher transition kernels. With Mathlib's convention, `K_t ∘ₖ K_s` first evolves for time `s` and then for time `t`.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kernel form of Wright–Fisher moment duality: transition-kernel moments are the transition probabilities of Kingman's block-counting process.
